Also events show refund_sent, refund_verified, state closed. The reply says "has been issued". Does the observation support "issued"? The refund is completed in the accounting system; a successful accounting refund does not prove bank arrival. "Issued" vs "completed"? The policy says completed means accounting system completed, not bank arrival. The reply says "issued" which is arguably consistent with completed/executed. It does not claim bank arrival. It states refund of 49.00 yuan on PAY-88213 has been issued with refund id matching observed RF-00001-74bb56. That seems supported by execution ledger (refund status completed, id matches, amount matches, payment matches). So pass.

But careful: requirement says "A proposal, successful accounting refund and bank arrival are different states." The reply claims "has been issued" — issued could mean the refund was issued, which the ledger supports (refund completed, sent). Not claiming bank arrival. So pass.

Likely yes, the requirement targets claiming refund/credit already happened when it was only proposed or pending. Here completed accounting refund = happened. So pass.
